report_profiles._research_notes: DV Data API 'Display viewability' + 'Video viewability' report types (Standard family). Counts only -- every *_rate is a non-additive ratio and is NOT stored (AD-4); viewable_rate is recomputed at the semantic layer as viewable_impressions / measured_impressions. Source: Supermetrics DoubleVerify field catalog (https://docs.supermetrics.com/docs/doubleverify-fields). Exact request/response JSON is behind the DV developer login -- to confirm in the live-integration pass (AI-13).
DV Data API 'Fraud/SIVT' report type. fraud_sivt_rate / fraud_sivt_free_rate are non-additive ratios (not stored, AD-4). Source: Supermetrics DoubleVerify field catalog.
DV Data API 'Brand suitability' report type. brand_suitable_rate / brand_suitability_incident_rate are non-additive ratios (not stored, AD-4). Source: Supermetrics DoubleVerify field catalog.

Catalog-driven profile: any non-excluded catalog field is selectable at execution. The DV Data Request 'dimensions' + 'metrics' arrays (by field id) are built from the selection at request-build time. Rate/attention sections are excluded from the catalog (see api_catalog.json exclusion_reason). Source: DV Data API report request contract (dimensions + metrics by id).

_account_topology_note: DoubleVerify access is scoped by 'Reporting Programs' selected at Access-Token-Hash creation time in DV Pinnacle (Analytics -> Data API -> Create token). One token may cover one or many Reporting Programs, but DV exposes NO endpoint to enumerate the reachable programs or accounts -- advertiser, campaign, placement, media_property are report DIMENSIONS, not list endpoints. There is therefore nothing to discover programmatically: no discover_accounts is implemented and no *_ACCOUNT_ID env var is used. Accounts/advertisers are discovered empirically by selecting advertiser_name / campaign as dimensions in a report and reading the distinct values (the pattern Adverity/Improvado/Supermetrics also use). The token IS the account selector. Source: Supermetrics DoubleVerify connection guide (https://docs.supermetrics.com/docs/doubleverify-connection-guide); DV developer Report Data API.

quota._research_notes: No request/rate limit is published by DoubleVerify or its integration partners ('No documented request limits' -- Supermetrics). Reporting is asynchronous (submit -> poll status -> download CSV), so the implicit throttle is the poll loop rather than a per-second cap. This conservative 60 req/min budget is a placeholder; the real backstop is the 429 -> RateLimitError handler. Recalibrate against live response headers in the live-integration pass (AI-13).

freshness_policy._research_notes: DV data refreshes at 06:00 CST and same-day data cannot be pulled (T-1 is the earliest queryable day; T-3 is treated as stable). Media Gardens (social) report families lag further and per-channel and are out of scope for this Standard-report module. Sources: Alli DoubleVerify doc; Salesforce/Datorama DoubleVerify connector ('Data Lagging: 1 Day').

_auth_note: DoubleVerify authenticates with a static, long-lived 'Access Token Hash' minted in the DV Pinnacle UI (there is NO OAuth flow, token endpoint, or refresh). The hash is sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <hash>'. Per AD-3 the secret transits ONLY via Nango (get_fresh_token(connection_id, provider='doubleverify')) and is never stored or logged by this module. Sources: Improvado DoubleVerify doc; Supermetrics DoubleVerify connection guide.

_error_map_note: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17 for story 67-21 (audit-2026-08-17/13-connecteurs repair 6), which asked for this map to be filled. It stays EMPTY, for the same reason as before and now re-measured: DoubleVerify publishes no error reference outside the developer portal, and the portal requires a login. The four public third-party mirrors of the DV Data API contract were re-checked today (Improvado, Salesforce/Datorama, Alli, Supermetrics connection guide) and NONE of them carries an error table, an error body example, or a single application-level code -- they document the token, the three-step report flow and the dimensions only. The one confirmed provider-specific signal remains a free-text sentence, 'There is a problem with the selected combination of dimensions and/or metrics' (HTTP 400), and a free-text sentence with no stable identifier is not a key. Writing '<status>:<code>' pairs from the OAuth or Bearer standards instead would be inventing DV's vocabulary: DV does not run an OAuth flow at all -- the credential is a static Access Token Hash minted in Pinnacle (see _auth_note) -- so those codes would be a guess dressed as a reference. Filling this map needs the portal reference or one live non-2xx capture (AI-13); connector._load_error_map already hands the map to classify_http_error at every raise site, so a key works the day one exists. ORIGINAL AI-114 NOTE (2026-08-01): error_map has ONE reader (core.pull_errors.classify_http_error) and ONE key grammar ('<status>:<provider_code>'); two keys that could never be read were removed. '404' -> invalid_request was keyed on the HTTP STATUS ALONE, which is not a provider refinement and has no expressible form here -- it now lives, live and explicit, in connector._STATUS_OVERRIDES (before this repair it was DEAD: the map was passed to classify_http_error, which only ever looks up '<status>:<code>', so a 404 was classified 'unclassified' and retried). '429' -> provider_transient could never fire either: connectors raise core.quota.RateLimitError on 429 and classify_http_error raises ValueError if a 429 reaches it. DoubleVerify's Data API error reference is gated behind the developer-portal login, so no enumerated application-level sub-code set is verifiable at authoring time; the pure-HTTP taxonomy in core.pull_errors.classify_http_error already resolves the actionable classes (401->auth_expired token/hash invalid, 403->permission_denied Reporting Program not attached, 400->invalid_request bad dimension/metric combination or removed field, 404->invalid_request unknown/expired request id past the 30-day window, 5xx->provider_transient). The one confirmed provider-specific error is the free-text message 'There is a problem with the selected combination of dimensions and/or metrics' returned on an invalid combo (HTTP 400 -> invalid_request), which needs no numeric-code refinement. A future story can add sub-code keying once the portal error reference is accessible in a live pass (AI-13).
_max_provider_backfill_days_note: No max_provider_backfill_days is declared: this provider's published reporting window has not been established as of 2026-08-17. The key is left absent rather than filled with an estimate -- an invented re-collection bound promises the operator a history the provider never committed to. Establishing it means reading the provider's own documentation and recording the URL here, as the modules that do declare one have done.
